fr.L: et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a ordonné de prêcher au peuple et d’attester que c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui a été désigné par Dieu [comme] juge des vivants et des morts.
fr.B: Il nous a ordonné de l’annoncer au peuple et d’attester solennellement que c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} que Dieu a établi juge des vivants et des morts.
fr.R: Jésus nous a dit de prêcher au peuple. Il nous a dit d’expliquer clairement que Dieu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a choisi pour juger tous les gens, ceux qui sont vivants et ceux qui sont morts.

decisions.choice: he commanded: the risen Jesus gave the command
decisions.reason: The subject could be God, the subject of 10:40. But the command to the witnesses comes from Jesus after he rose (1:2, 1:8; Luke 24:47-48).

decisions.choice: the people: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: As in 10:41; the message then reaches the Gentiles too, as here in Cornelius's house.

decisions.choice: appointed by God as judge of the living and the dead: Jesus will judge all people, at his coming
decisions.reason: Paul says the same in Athens (17:31). "The living and the dead" means everyone who has ever lived (2 Timothy 4:1, 1 Peter 4:5).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject, as the meaning note explains, and marks the choice as uncertain.

decisions.choice: the judge of all people, those who are alive and those who have died
alternatives: judge of the living and the dead
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pair means.

source.text: τούτῳ πάντες οἱ προφῆται μαρτυροῦσιν, ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν λαβεῖν διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ πάντα τὸν πιστεύοντα εἰς αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: To this one all the prophets bear witness, forgiveness of sins to receive through the name of him everyone the [one] believing in him.

en.L: To {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all the prophets bear witness, that everyone who believes in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} receives forgiveness of sins through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name."
en.B: Every one of the prophets bears witness to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: whoever believes in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} has their sins forgiven through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name."
en.R: All the prophets wrote about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They said that God forgives the sins of everyone who believes in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because of who Jesus is and what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done."

fr.L: À {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} tous les prophètes rendent témoignage : quiconque croit en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} reçoit par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom le pardon des péchés. »
fr.B: Tous les prophètes, sans exception, témoignent de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} : celui qui croit en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} voit ses péchés pardonnés grâce à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom. »
fr.R: Tous les prophètes ont parlé de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Ils ont dit que Dieu pardonne les péchés de tous ceux qui croient en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, à cause de ce que Jésus est et de ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait. »

decisions.choice: all the prophets bear witness: the Scriptures as a whole point to Jesus
decisions.reason: Peter does not quote one text. Jesus taught that the law, the prophets and the psalms speak of him (Luke 24:27, 24:44-47), and Peter said all the prophets announced these days (3:18, 3:24). Isaiah 53:5-6, 53:11 and Jeremiah 31:34 speak of sins taken away.

decisions.choice: through his name: through who he is and what he has done
alternatives: by saying his name as a formula
decisions.reason: The name stands for the person, as in 3:16 and 4:12.

decisions.choice: everyone who believes in him: anyone at all, Jew or Gentile
decisions.reason: "Everyone" is the point of this speech: God has no favorites (10:34). As Peter says it, the Spirit falls on his Gentile hearers (10:44).

decisions.choice: because of who Jesus is and what he has done
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom, as the meaning note does.

decisions.choice: God forgives the sins
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who forgives.

source.text: Ἔτι λαλοῦντος τοῦ Πέτρου τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα ἐπέπεσε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντας τὸν λόγον.

records.literal_gloss: Still speaking the Peter the words these fell the Spirit the Holy upon all those hearing the word.

en.L: While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all who were hearing the word.
en.B: Peter was still saying these things when the Holy Spirit came down on everyone who was listening to the message.
en.R: Peter was still speaking when the Holy Spirit came on all the people who were listening to the message.

fr.L: Pierre prononçant encore ces paroles, l’Esprit Saint tomba sur tous ceux qui entendaient la parole.
fr.B: Pierre parlait encore quand l’Esprit Saint descendit sur tous ceux qui écoutaient le message.
fr.R: Pierre parlait encore quand l’Esprit Saint est venu sur tous les gens qui écoutaient son message.

decisions.choice: fell upon: came suddenly and powerfully
decisions.reason: Peter says in 11:15 that the Spirit fell on them as on the apostles at the beginning (2:1-4). It happened before Peter had finished, and before anyone was baptized or had hands laid on them (compare 8:17).

decisions.choice: the word: the message about Jesus that Peter was speaking
decisions.reason: As in 10:36 and 4:4, "the word" is the message of the gospel.

decisions.choice: came down on / came on
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a plainer verb; Literal keeps "fell", the word Peter repeats in 11:15.

source.text: καὶ ἐξέστησαν οἱ ἐκ περιτομῆς πιστοὶ ὅσοι συνῆλθαν τῷ Πέτρῳ, ὅτι καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ ἔθνη ἡ δωρεὰ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἐκκέχυται·

records.literal_gloss: And were amazed the from circumcision believers as many as came with the Peter, that also upon the Gentiles the gift of the Holy Spirit has been poured out;

en.L: And the believers from [the] circumcision who had come with Peter were amazed, because the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles;
en.B: The Jewish believers who had come with Peter were astonished that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out on Gentiles too.
en.R: The Jewish believers who had come with Peter were amazed. God had given the Holy Spirit as a gift even to people who were not Jews!

fr.L: Et les croyants issus de la circoncision, tous ceux qui étaient venus avec Pierre, furent stupéfaits de ce que le don de l’Esprit Saint avait été répandu aussi sur les nations ;
fr.B: Les croyants juifs qui étaient venus avec Pierre furent stupéfaits de voir que le don de l’Esprit Saint était répandu aussi sur les non-Juifs.
fr.R: Les croyants juifs venus avec Pierre étaient très étonnés. Dieu avait donné l’Esprit Saint en cadeau, même à des gens qui n’étaient pas juifs !

decisions.choice: the believers from the circumcision: Jewish believers
alternatives: a party that insisted on circumcision
decisions.reason: Here the phrase simply means the believers who were Jews by birth, the brothers from Joppa (10:23). In 11:2 a similar phrase names those in Jerusalem who objected.

decisions.choice: poured out: the words of Joel's prophecy
decisions.reason: Peter quoted Joel at Pentecost: God will pour out his Spirit on all flesh (2:17-18, 2:33; Joel 3:1-2 in the Hebrew numbering). Now that includes Gentiles.

decisions.choice: the gift of the Holy Spirit: the gift that is the Spirit himself
decisions.reason: As in 2:38; 11:17 says God gave them the same gift.

decisions.choice: people who were not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable explains "Gentiles".

decisions.choice: God had given the Holy Spirit as a gift
alternatives: the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the giver, as the passive implies, and puts the gift as the Spirit himself.

decisions.choice: les nations (L); les non-Juifs (B); des gens qui n’étaient pas juifs (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles for the New Testament. "Les païens" now suggests people without religion, which Cornelius was not; Readable explains the word, as the English does.

source.text: ἤκουον γὰρ αὐτῶν λαλούντων γλώσσαις καὶ μεγαλυνόντων τὸν θεόν.

records.literal_gloss: they were hearing for them speaking in tongues and magnifying the God.

en.L: for they heard them speaking in tongues and magnifying God.
en.B: For they heard them speaking in tongues and praising the greatness of God.
en.R: They knew this because they heard these people speaking in tongues, as the believers did at Pentecost, and praising God for how great {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is.

fr.L: car ils les entendaient parler en langues et magnifier Dieu.
fr.B: En effet, ils les entendaient parler en langues et célébrer la grandeur de Dieu.
fr.R: Ils le savaient parce qu’ils entendaient ces gens parler en langues, comme les croyants à la Pentecôte, et louer Dieu pour {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grandeur.

decisions.choice: speaking in tongues: speech given by the Spirit, as at Pentecost
decisions.reason: At Pentecost the believers spoke in languages that hearers from many nations understood (2:4-11). Peter says these Gentiles received the same gift as the apostles at the beginning (11:15, 11:17), but Luke does not say whether anyone here understood the languages.

decisions.choice: magnifying God: praising God's greatness
decisions.reason: The verb means to declare great, as in Luke 1:46. At Pentecost too the believers spoke of the mighty works of God (2:11).

decisions.choice: as the believers did at Pentecost
decisions.reason: Readable draws the link that Peter himself draws in 11:15.

source.text: τότε ἀπεκρίθη Πέτρος·

records.literal_gloss: Then answered Peter,

en.L: Then Peter answered,
en.B: Then Peter said,
en.R: Then Peter said,

fr.L: Alors Pierre répondit :
fr.B: Alors Pierre dit :
fr.R: Alors Pierre a dit :

decisions.choice: answered: responded to what had happened
decisions.reason: No one had asked anything. The verb often means to respond to a situation, here to the Spirit's coming.

decisions.choice: said
decisions.reason: Since no one asked a question, Balanced and Readable say "said".

source.text: Μήτι τὸ ὕδωρ δύναται κωλῦσαί τις τοῦ μὴ βαπτισθῆναι τούτους οἵτινες τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἔλαβον ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς;

records.literal_gloss: Not the water is able to forbid anyone, the not to be baptized these, who the Spirit the Holy received as also we?

en.L: "Can anyone withhold the water, so that these should not be baptized, who have received the Holy Spirit just as we also [did]?"
en.B: "Surely no one can refuse the water to keep these people from being baptized. They have received the Holy Spirit just as we did!"
en.R: "These people have received the Holy Spirit, just as we did. So no one can stop them from being baptized with water!"

fr.L: « Quelqu’un peut-il refuser l’eau, pour que ne soient pas baptisés ceux-ci, qui ont reçu l’Esprit Saint tout comme nous ? »
fr.B: « Personne, assurément, ne peut refuser l’eau et empêcher ces gens d’être baptisés. Ils ont reçu l’Esprit Saint tout comme nous ! »
fr.R: « Ces gens ont reçu l’Esprit Saint, comme nous. Alors personne ne peut les empêcher d’être baptisés dans l’eau ! »

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer no: no one can refuse them baptism
decisions.reason: The Greek form of the question expects "no". Peter recalls this in 11:17: who was he to stand in God's way?

decisions.choice: who have received the Holy Spirit just as we did: God has already accepted them
decisions.reason: Peter reasons from what God has done. In 15:8-9 he says God gave them the Spirit and made no distinction between them and the Jews.

decisions.choice: withhold: forbid, prevent
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in 8:36 and 11:17, and of children in Luke 18:16.

decisions.choice: a statement rather than a question
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the answer the question expects.

source.text: προσέταξεν δὲ αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ βαπτισθῆναι.

records.literal_gloss: He commanded and them in the name of Jesus Christ to be baptized.

en.L: And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: So he gave orders for them to be baptized in the name of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: So Peter told them to be baptized in the name of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

fr.L: Et il ordonna qu’ils soient baptisés au nom de Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Il donna donc l’ordre de les baptiser au nom de Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.
fr.R: Alors Pierre leur a dit de se faire baptiser au nom de Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.

decisions.choice: in the name of Jesus Christ: calling on Jesus and coming under his authority
decisions.reason: As in 2:38 and 8:16.

decisions.choice: he commanded them to be baptized: Peter gave the order; others may have baptized them
decisions.reason: The Greek says Peter ordered it, not who did it, as Paul often left baptizing to others (1 Corinthians 1:14-17).

decisions.choice: Christ, with "Messiah" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As everywhere.

source.text: τότε ἠρώτησαν αὐτὸν ἐπιμεῖναι ἡμέρας τινάς.

records.literal_gloss: Then they asked him to remain days some.

en.L: Then they asked him to stay some days.
en.B: Then they asked him to stay on with them for a few days.
en.R: Then they asked Peter to stay with them for a few more days.

fr.L: Alors ils lui demandèrent de rester quelques jours.
fr.B: Ils le prièrent alors de demeurer quelques jours avec eux.
fr.R: Ensuite, ils ont demandé à Pierre de rester encore quelques jours avec eux.

decisions.choice: to stay some days: as their guest, eating and lodging in a Gentile house
decisions.reason: Staying with Gentiles is what the believers in Jerusalem criticized: "you went in to uncircumcised men and ate with them" (11:3).
